coffee-sales.title: What sales volume and revenue did the business record?
coffee-sales.code:
SELECT SUM(sales) as total_revenue, SUM(quantity) as units_sold, COUNT(DISTINCT orderid) AS distinct_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT customerid) as purchasing_customers
FROM orders
coffee-sales.explanation: SUM totals sales and quantities. COUNT DISTINCT prevents repeated order and customer IDs inflating those KPIs.
coffee-sales.finding: 45,135.35 across 957 orders is the sales baseline. The 3,551 units measure volume independently of order count.
coffee-sales.decision: Use the baseline to compare sales performance across periods.
coffee-sales.action: Review revenue, units and order counts together each month.

coffee-sales.title: Which coffee types lead revenue and unit sales?
coffee-sales.code:
SELECT SUM(sales) AS revenue, SUM(quantity) units_sold, coffeetypename
FROM orders
GROUP BY coffeetypename
ORDER BY revenue DESC
coffee-sales.explanation: GROUP BY coffee type supports separate comparisons of SUM(sales) and SUM(quantity).
coffee-sales.finding: Excelsa leads revenue at 12,306.71. Comparing revenue with units helps separate product value from volume.
coffee-sales.decision: Decide which coffee types warrant an inventory review.
coffee-sales.action: Compare demand with stock availability and margins before adjusting stock.
coffee-sales.kpi: Units sold and stockout rate by coffee type

coffee-sales.title: Which markets contribute the most coffee revenue?
coffee-sales.code:
SELECT country, SUM(sales) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT orderid), COUNT(DISTINCT customerid) , ROUND(SUM(sales)/ COUNT(DISTINCT orderid),2) AS AverageOrderValue
FROM orders
GROUP by country
coffee-sales.explanation: The query groups by country, counts distinct invoices and customers, and divides revenue by each market’s order count.
coffee-sales.finding: The United States contributes 35,639.73, about 79% of revenue. A large share of sales depends on one market.
coffee-sales.decision: Decide where to examine sales concentration first.
coffee-sales.action: Track market shares and investigate demand in smaller markets before expanding.

online-retail.title: What revenue, orders, customers and order value did retail record?
online-retail.code:
WITH revenue_summary AS(    
    SELECT 
        SUM(Revenue) AS total_revenue, 
        COUNT (DISTINCT Invoice) AS total_orders, 
        COUNT (DISTINCT CustomerID) AS total_customers
    FROM OnlineRetail..OnlineRetail)
SELECT 
    ROUND(total_revenue,2) AS total_revenue,
    total_orders,
    total_customers,
    ROUND(total_revenue/total_orders,2) AS average_order_value
FROM revenue_summary
online-retail.explanation: A CTE aggregates sales and counts distinct invoices and customers before calculating average order value.
online-retail.finding: The cleaned dataset contains 17,743,429.18 in positive sales over 36,969 distinct invoices. These totals exclude returns.
online-retail.decision: Set a baseline for retail reporting.
online-retail.action: Track positive sales separately from returns and net revenue.

online-retail.title: Which countries contribute the most retail revenue?
online-retail.code:
SELECT
    Country,
    ROUND (SUM(Revenue),2) AS Revenue,
    COUNT (DISTINCT Invoice) AS Orders,
    COUNT (DISTINCT CustomerID) AS Customers
FROM OnlineRetail..OnlineRetail
GROUP BY Country
ORDER BY revenue DESC
online-retail.explanation: GROUP BY Country measures market revenue and distinct counts at the same level.
online-retail.finding: The UK generated about 82.98% of retained sales revenue. Other markets account for a much smaller share.
online-retail.decision: Prioritise a review of exposure to the UK market.
online-retail.action: Monitor the country mix and investigate non-UK demand before making expansion decisions.

online-retail.title: Which stock-code and description combinations lead sales?
online-retail.code:
SELECT 
    StockCode,
    Description,
    ROUND(SUM(revenue),2) AS Revenue,
    SUM(Quantity) AS Units_Sold,
    COUNT (DISTINCT Invoice) AS Orders
FROM OnlineRetail..OnlineRetail
WHERE StockCode is not null
GROUP BY StockCode, Description
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
online-retail.explanation: Groups by both stock code and description, then ranks revenue. A stock code can appear under different descriptions.
online-retail.finding: The leading row is stock code 22423. Revenue rankings should be read alongside volumes and stock-code definitions.
online-retail.decision: Identify products to examine for assortment and inventory planning.
online-retail.action: Group consistently by stock code and separate nonmerchandise entries before changing the assortment.
online-retail.kpi: Units sold and revenue by stock code

hr-analytics.title: What is the overall employee attrition rate?
hr-analytics.code:
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS total_employees,
    SUM(attrition_flag) AS employees_left,
    ROUND(100 * SUM(attrition_flag) / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_percentage
FROM hr_analysis;
hr-analytics.explanation: SUM counts leavers via the CASE-derived flag. COUNT counts employees. The original integer expression truncates before ROUND.
hr-analytics.finding: 237 of 1,470 employees left. The decimal snapshot baseline is 16.12%.
hr-analytics.decision: Set a baseline for comparing groups.
hr-analytics.action: Compare future snapshots using the same definition.

hr-analytics.title: Which departments have the highest employee attrition rates?
hr-analytics.code:
SELECT 
    Department,
    COUNT(*) AS total_employees,
    SUM(attrition_flag) AS employees_left,
    ROUND(100 * SUM(attrition_flag) / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_percentage
FROM hr_analysis
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY attrition_percentage DESC;
hr-analytics.explanation: SUM counts leavers via the CASE-derived flag. COUNT counts employees. The original integer expression truncates before ROUND.
hr-analytics.finding: Sales has the highest decimal rate at 20.63%, followed by Human Resources at 19.05%. Research & Development has the most leavers in absolute terms (133).
hr-analytics.decision: Use both rates and counts to prioritise investigation.
hr-analytics.action: Review workload and employee feedback in Sales, and examine the volume of departures in R&D.
hr-analytics.kpi: Department attrition rate and leaver count

hr-analytics.title: Which job roles show the highest attrition rates?
hr-analytics.code:
SELECT
    JobRole,
    COUNT(*) AS total_employees,
    SUM(attrition_flag) AS employees_left,
    ROUND(100 * SUM(attrition_flag) / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_percentage
FROM hr_analysis
GROUP BY JobRole
ORDER BY attrition_percentage DESC;
hr-analytics.explanation: SUM counts leavers via the CASE-derived flag. COUNT counts employees. The original integer expression truncates before ROUND.
hr-analytics.finding: Sales Representatives have the highest observed rate. Group sizes differ across roles and affect the interpretation.
hr-analytics.decision: Identify roles that warrant a closer retention review.
hr-analytics.action: Ask HR to investigate job conditions and compare rates alongside role headcounts.
hr-analytics.kpi: Attrition rate and headcount by role

hr-analytics.title: How does overtime relate to employee attrition?
hr-analytics.code:
SELECT
    OverTime,
    COUNT(*) AS total_employees,
    SUM(attrition_flag) AS employees_left,
    ROUND(100 * SUM(attrition_flag) / COUNT(*), 2) AS attrition_percentage
FROM hr_analysis
GROUP BY OverTime
ORDER BY attrition_percentage DESC;
hr-analytics.explanation: SUM counts leavers via the CASE-derived flag. COUNT counts employees. The original integer expression truncates before ROUND.
hr-analytics.finding: The decimal rate is 30.53% with overtime and 10.44% without. The comparison is observational.
hr-analytics.decision: Decide whether workload patterns warrant review.
hr-analytics.action: Compare overtime allocation with role, staffing and employee feedback.
